subject: Chemistry
cards: OCR-H432.IONIC_BONDING

What is meant by ionic bonding?

[1 mark]

(Electrostatic) **attraction** between **oppositely** charged **OR** + and - **ions**
Ignore: references to metal and non-metal
Note: **Attraction** is essential
OCR-H432.ACID

What is meant by an acid?

[1 mark]

(Acid) releases H+ ions/ H+ donor
Also accept: H+ OR proton
OCR-H432.WEAK_ACID

What is meant by an acid that is weak?

[1 mark]

(weak acid) partially dissociates/ionises
Ignore: vague responses that do not imply a number, e.g. poor proton donor
Ignore: ‘doesn’t easily dissociate’
Ignore: ‘strong acid completely dissociates’
OCR-H432.STRONG_ACID

What is meant by a strong acid?

[1 mark]

(Strong acid) completely/fully dissociates/ionises
Also accept: ALL H+ ions are released
Not accepted: easily dissociates
OCR-H432.DISPROPORTIONATION

What is meant by the term disproportionation?

[1 mark]

Oxidation and reduction of the same **element**
Also accept: ‘chlorine’ OR ‘Cl’ for same element
Not accepted: ‘Atom’ is insufficient for element
Ignore: ‘species’ for ‘element’
OCR-H432.COVALENT_BOND

What is meant by a covalent bond?

[1 mark]

Shared pair of electrons
Ignore: comments about attraction between nuclei and shared pair OR magnetic attraction
OCR-H432.STANDARD_SOLUTION

What is meant by the term standard solution?

[1 mark]

A solution of known concentration
Also accept: description of concentration
OCR-H432.ALKALI

Explain what is meant by an alkali.

[1 mark]

releases OH-/hydroxide (ions in aqueous solution)
Also accept: containing/forms OH- (ions)
Also accept: ionises to give OH- (ions)
Ignore: mention of pH
OCR-H432.RELATIVE_ATOMIC_MASS_OF_AN_ELEMENT

Explain what is meant by the term relative atomic mass of an element.

[2 marks]

• (Weighted) mean/average mass of an **atom**
• compared with 1/12th mass of carbon-12
• OR compared with mass of carbon-12 which is 12
Also accept: mass of 1 mole of atoms compared to 1/12th 1 mole/12 g of carbon-12
Also accept: mass of one mole of atoms 1/12th mass of one mole/12 g of carbon-12
Not accepted: mean mass of an element
Note: i.e. ‘atom’ essential
OCR-H432.ELECTRONEGATIVITY

What is meant by the term electronegativity?

[2 marks]

• The ability/tendency of an atom to attract electrons
• in a covalent bond
Also accept: ‘attraction of an atom for electrons’
Also accept: ‘pull’ for ‘attract’
Also accept: ‘shared pair’ or ‘bond(ing) pair’ for ‘covalent bond’
Not accepted: ‘element’ for ‘atom’
Not accepted: ability to attract an electron (i.e. reference to a single electron)
OCR-H432.ENTHALPY_CHANGE_OF_REACTION

What is meant by the term enthalpy change of reaction?

[1 mark]

(The enthalpy change) for the stated equation
Also accept: reaction in molar quantities/stoichiometric ratio as shown/stated/given/in equation
Not accepted: Energy released (can’t assume reaction is exothermic)
Ignore: standard states or conditions
OCR-H432.HOMOLYTIC_FISSION

Explain what is meant by homolytic fission.

[1 mark]

• (covalent/Br-Br) bond breaks
• AND
• each (bonding) atom / Br receives one electron from the bonding / shared pair
Also accept: the breaking of (a covalent/Br-Br) bond where each atom keeps one of the bonding electrons
Also accept: when a bond breaks one electron from the bond goes to each product / species / radical
Not accepted: ‘molecule’ or ‘compound’ or ‘particle’ or ‘element’ for ‘atom’
Ignore: homolytic fission equations
OCR-H432.RADICAL

What is meant by a radical?

[1 mark]

A species with an unpaired electron
Not accepted: species with one electron
OCR-H432.ENTHALPY_CHANGE_OF_HYDRATION

Explain what is meant by the term enthalpy change of hydration.

[2 marks]

• (enthalpy change when)
• 1 mole of gaseous ions react
• OR 1 mole of hydrated/aqueous ions are formed
• gaseous ions dissolve in **water**
• OR gaseous ions form aqueous/hydrated ions
Ignore: ‘energy released’ OR ‘energy required’
OCR-H432.AVERAGE_BOND_ENTHALPY

Explain what is meant by the term average bond enthalpy.

[2 marks]

• **Average bond enthalpy**
• Breaking of one mole of bonds
• In gaseous molecules
Not accepted: bonds formed
Not accepted: ionic bonds
Ignore: energy required OR energy released
Ignore: heterolytic / homolytic
Ignore: species for molecules
OCR-H432.LATTICE_ENTHALPY

Define the term lattice enthalpy.

[2 marks]

• (Enthalpy / heat energy change / released when) 1 mol of (ionic lattice)
• Is formed from its gaseous ions
Also accept: 1 mol of (ionic) compound/product/substance
Also accept: M+(g) + X-(g) → MX(s)
Not accepted: one mole of gaseous ions
Ignore: energy released/required
OCR-H432.MONODENTATE_LIGAND

What is meant by a monodentate ligand?

[1 mark]

• **Donates** one/an electron pair (to a metal ion)
• AND forms one/a dative (covalent) / coordinate bond (to a metal ion)
Also accept: lone pair for electron pair
OCR-H432.WEIGHTED_MEAN_MASS

Explain what is meant by the term weighted mean mass.

[1 mark]

(The mean/average mass) taking into account the relative abundancies of the isotopes
Also accept: sum of (isotopic mass × %abundance)
Also accept: sum of (isotopic mass × abundance) / total abundance
Not accepted: average mass of the isotopes
OCR-H432.ENTHALPY_CHANGE_OF_SOLUTION

Explain what is meant by enthalpy change of solution.

[1 mark]

(enthalpy change for) **1 mole** of a compound/substance/solid/solute **dissolving**
Also accept: For dissolving, forms aqueous/hydrated ions
Not accepted: dissolving elements
Not accepted: response that implies formation of 1 mole of aqueous ions
Ignore: ‘energy released’ OR ‘energy required’
Ignore: ionic OR covalent
OCR-H432.STEREOISOMERS

Define the term stereoisomers.

[1 mark]

• Same structural formula
• AND
• Different arrangement (of atoms) **in space OR** different **spatial** arrangement (of atoms)
Also accept: have the same structure/displayed formula/skeletal formula
Not accepted: same empirical formula OR same general formula
Not accepted: Reference to E/Z isomerism or optical isomerism is not sufficient
Ignore: same molecular formula
OCR-H432.STRUCTURAL_ISOMERS

What is meant by the term structural isomers?

[1 mark]

• Same **molecular** formula
• AND
• Different **structural** formulae
• OR
• Both have the **molecular** formula C6H12
• AND
• Different **structural** formulae
Also accept: For ‘structural formulae’, structure/displayed/skeletal formulae/ functional groups
Not accepted: any reference to spatial/space
Not accepted: Same formula is not sufficient (no reference to molecular)
Not accepted: Different arrangement of atoms is not sufficient (no reference to structure/structural)
OCR-H432.ELECTROPHILE

What is meant by the term electrophile?

[1 mark]

An electron pair acceptor
Also accept: gains an electron pair / lone pair
OCR-H432.BIDENTATE_LIGAND

Explain what is meant by the term bidentate ligand.

[2 marks]

• species with **two lone pairs** (of electrons)
• forming **dative** (covalent)/**co-ordinate bond(s)**
• OR
• **donates electrons** to a (central) **metal atom/ion**
Also accept: species with lone pairs that form two dative/coordinate bonds
Also accept: non-bonding pair for lone pair
Ignore: LP for lone pair
Ignore: donates two pairs of electrons alone
OCR-H432.NUCLEOPHILE

What is meant by the term nucleophile?

[1 mark]

Donates an electron **pair** (to another species)
Also accept: donates a lone pair
OCR-H432.R_3.1.2_CA_SR_WATER_RATE

Explain why calcium reacts more slowly with water than strontium does.

[3 marks]

• Atomic radius
• Ca has smaller atomic radius
• OR fewer shells
• Effect of nuclear charge/shielding
• Ca has **less/decreased** shielding
• Nuclear attraction
• Ca has greater nuclear attraction (for electrons)
• OR Ca has a higher ionisation energy
• OR more energy is required to lose the outer electrons
Also accept: ‘fewer energy levels’
Also accept: ‘electrons closer to nucleus’
Also accept: more electron repulsion from inner shells
Also accept: ‘less nuclear pull’
Also accept: ‘electrons held less tightly’
Also accept: ORA in terms of Sr
Ignore: fewer orbitals OR fewer sub-shells OR different shell
Ignore: nuclear charge/effective nuclear charge
Note: Comparison needed for each mark.
OCR-H432.R_3.1.4_AMMONIUM_ION_TEST

Outline how you would test for the presence of NH4+ ions in a solution. Your answer should include observations.

[2 marks]

• Reagent and conditions
• (Heat with) hydroxide
• Observation
• pH/litmus/indicator paper turns blue/purple
Also accept: NaOH/KOH/Ca(OH)2/OH-
Not accepted: Ammonium hydroxide OR ammonia
OCR-H432.R_6.2.2_OPTICAL_ISOMERISM

Most α-amino acids show optical isomerism. Explain the term optical isomerism.

[1 mark]

Non-superimposable mirror images (about a chiral centre)
Ignore: definition of stereoisomers
OCR-H432.R_6.1.2_CARBONYL_TEST_2_4_DNPH

Describe a chemical test to confirm the presence of a carbonyl group. How could the product of this test be used to identify the carbonyl compound? Your answer should not include spectroscopy.

[3 marks]

• (Add) 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine AND orange/yellow/red precipitate
• Take melting point (of crystals)
• Compare to known values/database
Also accept: errors in spelling
Also accept: 2,4(-)DNP OR 2,4(-)DNPH
Also accept: Brady’s reagent or Brady’s Test
Also accept: solid OR crystals OR ppt as alternatives for precipitate
Not accepted: 2nd and 3rd marks for taking and comparing boiling points OR chromatograms
OCR-H432.R_2.1.1_ISOTOPE_DIFFERENCES

Most elements contain different isotopes. State two differences between isotopes of the same element.

[1 mark]

• Two correct responses from
• Different numbers of neutrons
• Different (atomic) masses/mass numbers
• Different **physical** properties
Also accept: different relative isotopic masses
Not accepted: different relative atomic masses
Not accepted: different chemical properties OR different properties
Ignore: heavier/lighter
Ignore: different abundancies
Note: Physical required
OCR-H432.R_2.2.2_NF3_BF3_SHAPES

Explain why NF3 and BF3 molecules have different shapes and bond angles.

[2 marks]

• NF3 has **3 bonded** pairs AND **1 lone** pair (of electrons) AND **lone pairs** repel **more** (than bonded pairs)
• BF3 has **three** bonded pairs (of electrons)
Also accept: lp for lone pair (of electrons)
Also accept: bp for bonding pair (of electrons)
Also accept: regions for electron pairs
Also accept: ‘bonds’ for ‘bonded pair’
Not accepted: ‘atoms repel’
Ignore: ‘electrons repel’
OCR-H432.R_6.2.5_RECRYSTALLISATION_METHOD

A student reacts phenol with nitric acid and sulfuric acid at 100 °C to form impure crystals of an organic compound, C. The student purifies the crystals by recrystallisation. Describe how the student could recrystallise the impure crystals to obtain a pure sample of C.

[3 marks]

• Dissolve in **hot** water/solvent
• **Minimum** amount of solvent
• Cool **AND** Filter **AND** (leave to) dry
Also accept: any solvent
Not accepted: adding of a drying agent (e.g. MgSO4)
Ignore: Initial filtering
Ignore: hot filtration to remove insoluble impurities
Note: All three needed
OCR-H432.R_2.2.1_BROMIDE_ELECTRON_CONFIG

Write the electron configuration of a bromide ion, in terms of sub-shells.

[1 mark]

1s22s22p63s23p63d104s24p6
Also accept: 3d after 4s2 or after 4p6, e.g. 1s22s22p63s23p64s23d104p6
Also accept: upper case D, etc and subscripts, e.g. ......4S23D1
Not accepted: [Ar] as shorthand for 1s22s22p63s23p6
OCR-H432.R_2.2.1_MAGNESIUM_ELECTRON_CONFIG

Write the electron configuration, in terms of sub-shells, of a magnesium atom.

[1 mark]

1s22s22p63s2
Also accept: upper case S and P, and subscripts, e.g. ......2S23P6
OCR-H432.R_3.1.2_STRONTIUM_WATER_EQUATION

Write an equation for the reaction of strontium with water.

[1 mark]

Sr + 2H2O → Sr(OH)2 + H2
Also accept: multiples
Ignore: state symbols (even if wrong)
OCR-H432.R_3.2.3_DYNAMIC_EQUILIBRIUM_FEATURES

State two features of a dynamic equilibrium.

[2 marks]

Two from:
• **rate** of forward reaction = **rate** of reverse reaction
• Concentrations (of reactants and products) do not change/are constant
• In a closed system/environment
Also accept: backward for reverse
Also accept: ‘nothing can leave/enter’
Not accepted: concentration of reactants = concentration of products
Ignore: reactions take place together/reversible reaction
OCR-H432.R_2.1.5_PLATINUM_OXIDATION_NUMBER_CISPLATIN

Cis-platin, PtCl2(NH3)2, is a complex of platinum which is used in cancer treatment. What is the oxidation number of platinum in cis-platin?

[1 mark]

+2
Also accept: 2+ OR +II
Also accept: Pt2+
Note: Sign required
OCR-H432.R_2.1.5_RUBIDIUM_CHLORATE_VII

What is the name of RbClO4?

[1 mark]

Rubidium chlorate(VII)
Also accept: Rubidium(I) chlorate(VII)
Also accept: Rubidium chloroate(VII)
Ignore: Rubidium (VII)chlorate
Ignore: Rubidium chlorate(IIV)
Ignore: Rubidium chlorate (7)
Ignore: Rubidium perchlorate
OCR-H432.R_2.1.5_SULFITE_SYSTEMATIC_NAME

What is the systematic name of a SO3 2- ion?

[1 mark]

sulfate(IV) (ion)
Also accept: sulphate(IV)
Also accept: sulfite OR sulphite
Not accepted: ’oxide’ in name: e.g. sulfur trioxide OR sulfur(IV) oxide
OCR-H432.R_2.1.4_BARIUM_HYDROXIDE_HCL_EQUATION

Barium chloride can be prepared from barium hydroxide in a neutralisation reaction. Write the equation for this reaction. State symbols are not required.

[1 mark]

Ba(OH)2 + 2HCl → BaCl2 + 2H2O
Also accept: multiples
Ignore: state symbols (even if wrong)
OCR-H432.R_4.2.1_ALCOHOL_TO_DIACID_OXIDATION

HO(CH2)4OH can be oxidised to form HOOC(CH2)2COOH. State the reagents and conditions and write an equation for this oxidation. In the equation, use [O] for the oxidising agent.

[3 marks]

• Reagents
• K2Cr2O7 AND acid AND reflux
• Equation
• HO(CH2)4OH + 4[O] → HOOC(CH2)2COOH + 2H2O
Also accept: Na2Cr2O7 OR Cr2O72-
Also accept: H2SO4 OR HCl OR H+
Also accept: words. e.g. ‘acidified dichromate’
Also accept: a small slip in formula for dichromate e.g KCr2O7
OCR-H432.R_2.1.5_MAGNESIUM_ETHANOIC_ACID_REDOX

A student adds magnesium metal to an aqueous solution of ethanoic acid, CH3COOH. A redox reaction takes place. Write the overall equation for this reaction and explain, in terms of oxidation numbers, which element has been oxidised and which element has been reduced.

[3 marks]

• Equation: Mg + 2CH3COOH → (CH3COO)2Mg + H2
• Oxidation: Mg from 0 to +2
• Reduction: H from +1 to 0
Also accept: Mg(CH3COO)2
Also accept: multiples
Also accept: 1 mark for correct oxidation numbers but incorrectly linked to redox
Ignore: Oxidation numbers in formulae
Ignore: state symbols
OCR-H432.R_2.1.2_PHOSPHINE_OXYGEN_EQUATION

Phosphine, PH3, reacts with oxygen gas to form phosphorus(V) oxide and water. Write the equation for this reaction.

[1 mark]

4PH3 + 8O2 → P4O10 + 6H2O
Also accept: multiples
Also accept: 2PH3 + 4O2 → P2O5 + 3H2O
Ignore: state symbols, even if wrong
OCR-H432.R_2.1.5_SODIUM_AZIDE_HALF_EQUATIONS

Sodium azide, NaN3, has been used in car airbags. The airbag inflates when the NaN3 decomposes to form nitrogen gas: 2NaN3(s) → 2Na(s) + 3N2(g). This is a redox reaction. Write half-equations for the reduction and oxidation processes that take place.

[2 marks]

• Reduction: Na+ + e- → Na
• Oxidation: 2N3- → 3N2 + 2e-
Also accept: multiples e.g. 2Na+ + 2e- → 2Na
Also accept: 1 mark for 2 correct equations but wrong way round
Ignore: state symbols
OCR-H432.R_3.1.3_CHLORINE_WATER_RISK

Chlorine is used to kill bacteria in drinking water. State one risk in using chlorine in drinking water.

[1 mark]

• toxic/poisonous
• OR
• forms chlorinated hydrocarbons
• OR
• forms carcinogenic compounds / toxic compounds
Ignore: ‘harmful’/’dangerous’
Ignore: chlorine is carcinogenic/causes cancer dangerous for health/causes breathing problems
OCR-H432.R_3.1.3_CHLORINE_WATER_PURPOSE

Chlorine is used to treat water in large-scale water treatment plants. Suggest why chlorine is added to water in large-scale water treatment plants.

[1 mark]

killing bacteria
Also accept: killing microorganisms / microbes / sterilises water
Ignore: ‘removing’ bacteria
OCR-H432.R_3.1.3_HALIDE_TEST_REAGENT

Precipitation reactions can be used to distinguish between halide ions. State the reagent needed for these precipitation reactions.

[1 mark]

Silver nitrate OR AgNO3
Also accept: Ag+
Ignore: an incorrect formula if name correct
Ignore: acidified/HNO3
OCR-H432.R_4.1.2_BUTANE_PENTANE_BOILING_POINT

Explain the difference in the boiling points of butane and pentane.

[2 marks]

• Chain length: interaction between molecules
• Chain length (in pentane) is longer
• AND
• more (surface) contact
• OR greater surface area/SA
• London forces: strength and energy
• **Stronger** / **more** London forces
• OR **more energy to break** London forces
Also accept: Assume the following for longer chain: larger/bigger molecule; more C (and H); more atoms; more electrons
Also accept: induced dipole(-dipole) interactions for London forces
Not accepted: ‘branching’ is a CON
Ignore: comments about packing
Ignore: van der Waals’/vdw forces
Note: Comparisons needed throughout
Note: ORA throughout
OCR-H432.R_4.1.2_RADICAL_SUBSTITUTION_LIMITS

State two limitations of using radical substitution in organic synthesis.

[2 marks]

• further substitution/s
• OR
• produces different termination products
• OR
• More than one termination step
• OR
• Mixture of products are formed
• substitution at different positions along chain
Also accept: dibromo/multibromo compounds formed OR an example of a further substitution product OR an example of a different termination product
Also accept: more than one hydrogen (atom) can be replaced
Also accept: radicals react with each other to form other products
Also accept: a hydrogen (atom) on a different carbon (atom) can be replaced
Ignore: references to separation of products
Ignore: references to atom economy or yield
OCR-H432.R_3.1.1_IE_MG_TO_AL

Explain why the general increase in first ionisation energies across Period 3 is not followed for Mg (Z = 12) to Al (Z = 13).

[2 marks]

• Sub-shells
• Mg electron is removed from (3)s
• AND
• Al electron is removed from (3)p
• Energy levels
• Al electron has a higher **energy**
• OR (3)p has higher energy than (3)s
Also accept: (2)s and (2)p
Also accept: response implying that orbitals/sub-shell changes from s to p
Not accepted: unpaired electron removed more easily (ORA)
Ignore: number before s and p
Ignore: comments about distance from nucleus
Ignore: ‘less energy to remove’
OCR-H432.R_3.1.1_S_BLOCK_NA_MG

Explain which block in the periodic table sodium and magnesium belong to.

[1 mark]

• s-block
• AND highest energy **or** outer **electron** is in a s orbital **or** s sub-shell
Also accept: ‘outer’ or ‘valence’ for ‘highest energy’
Not accepted: s shell / energy level
Ignore: electron configurations
OCR-H432.R_6.1.1_BENZENE_DELOCALISED_EVIDENCE

One piece of evidence for the delocalised model is that benzene does not decolourise aqueous bromine. Suggest two other pieces of evidence which support the delocalised model of benzene.

[2 marks]

(In the delocalised model):
• (C-C) bond length is between single (C-C) and double bond (C=C)
• OR all (C-C) bond lengths are the same
• (Enthalpy change of) hydrogenation is less exothermic (than expected)
Also accept: ‘less negative’ OR ‘more positive’ OR ‘less (heat) energy released’ for ‘less exothermic’
Also accept: comparison of values that show delocalised is less exothermic e.g. Kekulé is -360 delocalised is -208
Not accepted: enthalpy of hydration OR ΔhydH
Ignore: less susceptible to electrophilic attack (given in question)
Ignore: higher/lower
OCR-H432.R_3.2.1_ENTHALPY_COMBUSTION

Explain the term enthalpy change of combustion.

[2 marks]

• (The enthalpy change) for complete combustion
• of 1 mol (of substance)
Also accept: energy change for combustion in excess oxygen OR reacts in excess oxygen OR reacts completely in oxygen OR energy released during complete combustion OR energy change for combustion in excess air
Also accept: element OR compound OR reactant
Not accepted: atoms
Ignore: energy required
OCR-H432.R_3.2.1_COMBUSTION_EXPERIMENT_REASONS

Suggest two reasons, apart from measurement uncertainties, why the experimental value for ΔcH is less exothermic than the data book value.

[2 marks]

Any two from:
• Heat released to the surroundings
• Incomplete combustion OR incomplete reaction
• OR not everything burns
• Non-standard conditions
Also accept: heat loss
Ignore: reference to evaporation
OCR-H432.R_3.2.1_EXOTHERMIC_BONDS

Explain, in terms of bond breaking and bond forming, why a reaction can be exothermic.

[1 mark]

**More** energy is **released** by **forming** bonds than energy **required** when **breaking** bonds
Also accept: ‘bond breaking is endothermic’ AND ‘bond making is exothermic’
Also accept: within labelled energy diagram
Note: ORA
Note: Response needs link between energy, breaking and making bonds
OCR-H432.R_3.2.1_STANDARD_CONDITIONS

State the conditions of temperature and pressure used for standard enthalpy measurements.

[1 mark]

• 298 K/25ºC
• AND
• 100 kPa
Also accept: ‘a stated temperature’
Also accept: 1 × 105 Pa, 101 kPa, 1.01 × 105 Pa, 1 atm, 1 bar
OCR-H432.R_4.2.1_SECONDARY_ALCOHOL

Why is butan-2-ol classified as a secondary alcohol?

[1 mark]

• The -OH group is attached to a carbon that is attached to one hydrogen atom
• OR
• The -OH group is attached to a carbon that is attached to two C atoms/ alkyl groups/R groups
Also accept: alcohol/ hydroxyl/functional group for -OH
OCR-H432.R_6.3.2_NMR_DEUTERATED

Explain the use of two deuterated compounds in NMR spectroscopy.

[2 marks]

• CDCl3 used as a solvent
• D2O used to identify OH OR NH protons
Also accept: for 1 mark, D2O as a solvent
Note: Example and use required for each mark
OCR-H432.R_3.2.2_RATE_DECREASES_COLLISIONS

Zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid, HCl(aq), as shown in the following equation. Zn(s) + 2HCl(aq) → ZnCl2(aq) + H2(g) A student investigates the rate of this reaction. The graph shows that rate of reaction decreases over time. Explain why, in terms of collision theory.

[2 marks]

• Rate
• (Acid) **concentration** decreases.
• Collisions
• Fewer collisions per second
• OR less frequent collisions
Not accepted: ‘fewer collisions’ alone is not sufficient (no rate)
Ignore: amount of acid decreases, response must imply a volume and NOT area, e.g. fewer particles/molecules/ions in same space /volume
OCR-H432.R_4.2.3_PURIFY_2_BROMOBUTANE

The student mixes butan-2-ol, sodium bromide and sulfuric acid in a pear-shaped flask, and refluxes the mixture. After 1 hour, the mixture in the flask has separated into two layers: an aqueous layer and an organic layer. Describe the procedures the student would need to carry out to obtain a pure, dry sample of 2-bromobutane from this mixture.

[3 marks]

• Separating funnel (to separate aqueous and organic layers)
• Dry organic layer with anhydrous salt
• Distil and collect fraction at 91oC
Also accept: Use a drying agent
Also accept: appropriate example of an anhydrous salt e.g. MgSO4, CaCl2
OCR-H432.R_3.2.2_CATALYST_COMPARE_VARIABLES

Aqueous hydrogen peroxide, H2O2(aq), gradually decomposes to produce water and oxygen. A student plans to compare the rate of decomposition of H2O2 using different metal oxides as the catalyst. Suggest two variables which should be kept constant.

[2 marks]

• ANY two
• Amount of catalyst/metal oxide
• (allow same mass OR same moles)
• Temperature
• Volume of H2O2
• Concentration of H2O2
• Moles/amount of H2O2
• Pressure
• Surface area of catalyst
Not accepted: concentration/volume of catalyst/metal oxide
OCR-H432.R_4.2.4_INFRARED_EFFECT_ON_BONDS

State the effect infrared radiation has on covalent bonds.

[1 mark]

(causes bonds to) vibrate **more** (and absorb energy)
Not accepted: Bond breaking
OCR-H432.R_4.2.1_VITAMIN_C_SOLUBILITY

Vitamin C is extremely soluble in water. Suggest why vitamin C is extremely soluble in water.

[1 mark]

Hydrogen bonding AND **Many** OH/hydroxyl / hydroxy / alcohol
Also accept: 4 OH
Not accepted: OH-
OCR-H432.R_4.1.3_HBR_AS_ELECTROPHILE

Suggest how an HBr molecule can act as an electrophile.

[1 mark]
(The H atom of HBr) accepts a pair of electrons
OCR-H432.R_4.1.3_STEAM_HYDRATION_CATALYST

The reaction of 2-chloropropene with steam requires a catalyst. State a suitable catalyst for this reaction.

[1 mark]

H+/acid/H2SO4/H3PO4
Also accept: HCl
Ignore: (aq) OR ‘dilute’ OR concentrated
OCR-H432.R_4.2.2_HYDROLYSIS_RATE_MEASUREMENT

1-Iodopentane can also be hydrolysed by water using aqueous silver nitrate, with ethanol as the solvent. A student uses this method to compare the rates of hydrolysis of 1-iodopentane and 1-bromopentane. What measurement and observation would allow the student to compare the rates of hydrolysis?

[1 mark]
**Time** for **precipitate** to appear
OCR-H432.R_2.1.2_PHOSPHORUS_BROMINE_EQUATION

Write the equation for the reaction of phosphorus with bromine.

[1 mark]

P4 + 6Br2 → 4PBr3
Also accept: multiples
OCR-H432.R_2.1.2_MAGNESIUM_ACID_IONIC_EQUATION

Construct an ionic equation for the reaction of magnesium with an acid.

[1 mark]

Mg + 2H+ → Mg2+ + H2
Also accept: multiples
Also accept: Mg+2
Ignore: state symbols
OCR-H432.R_3.1.2_MAGNESIUM_OXYGEN_EQUATION

Magnesium reacts with oxygen in the air. Write the equation for this reaction.

[1 mark]

2Mg + O2 → 2MgO
Also accept: multiples e.g. Mg + 1/2 O2 → MgO
Ignore: state symbols even if wrong
OCR-H432.R_3.1.1_NICKEL_BLOCK

Nickel and gallium are in period 4 of the periodic table. Which block in the periodic table does nickel belong to?

[1 mark]
d-block
OCR-H432.R_2.1.2_ALUMINIUM_SULFIDE_WATER_EQUATION

Aluminium forms a sulfide, Al2S3. Al2S3 reacts with water to form aluminium hydroxide and hydrogen sulfide, H2S. Write an equation for the reaction of Al2S3 with water.

[1 mark]

Al2S3 + 6H2O → 2Al(OH)3 + 3H2S
Also accept: correct multiples
Ignore: state symbols
OCR-H432.R_2.1.2_POTASSIUM_PERCHLORATE_ALUMINIUM

A mixture of potassium perchlorate, KClO4, and aluminium is used in fireworks. When the firework ignites, KClO4 reacts with aluminium to form potassium chloride, KCl, and aluminium oxide, Al2O3. Write the balanced equation for this reaction. State symbols are not required.

[1 mark]

3KClO4 + 8Al → 3KCl + 4Al2O3
Also accept: multiples
OCR-H432.R_2.1.2_PCL5_AMMONIUM_CHLORIDE_EQUATION

When phosphorus(V) chloride, PCl5, and ammonium chloride are heated together, the compound P3N3Cl6 is formed, together with HCl gas. P3N3Cl6 has a cyclic structure, like the Kekulé structure of benzene. Write an equation for the reaction of PCl5 and ammonium chloride to form P3N3Cl6.

[1 mark]

3PCl5 + 3NH4Cl → P3N3Cl6 + 12HCl
Also accept: multiples
Ignore: state symbols, even if wrong
OCR-H432.R_4.1.3_SIGMA_PI_DIFFERENCE

Describe one difference between the σ bond and the π bond.

[1 mark]

Any **one** from:
• σ bond is between bonding atoms/nuclei AND π bond is above and below the bonding atoms/nuclei
• σ bond has direct/head-on overlap of orbitals AND π bond has sideways overlap
• π bond has a lower bond enthalpy / is weaker than a σ bond
• σ bond has electron density between bonding atoms AND π bond has electron density above and below bonding atoms
Ignore: the length of the σ bond and π bond
Ignore: the type of orbital for σ bond
OCR-H432.R_4.1.3_SIGMA_PI_MEANING

Explain what is meant by the terms σ-bond and π-bond.

[2 marks]

• σ-bond: Overlap of **orbitals** between (bonding) atoms
• π-bond: **Sideways** overlap of (adjacent) **p-orbitals**
Also accept: labelled diagrams
Not accepted: pi-orbital
Ignore: the type of orbital for σ-bond

2-chloropropanoic acid, CH3CHClCOOH, can be made by reacting propanoic acid with chlorine in a radical substitution reaction. State the conditions for the reaction.

OCR-H432.R_3.2.2_CATALYST_ENVIRONMENT

Explain how the use of catalysts is beneficial to the environment.

[1 mark]

• Lower temperature can be used (for the same yield)
• OR less energy demand / required to heat reaction
• OR less fossil fuels need to be burnt
• OR reduction in CO2
• OR catalyst can be reused
